Book Excerpt

Page 126

IF AND ONLY IF is a double indicator. It is a marriage between the sufficient and necessary families. A Romeo and Juliet situation, but with less murder. As soon as you see IF AND ONLY IF, throw down a Double Must Arrow: ↔

IF AND ONLY IF just means the two variables always go together, hand in hand. You should rejoice when you see it; it vastly simplifies the conditional relationship . IF AND ONLY IF is one conditional indicator, but it is made up of a member of the sufficient family and the necessary family.

It doesn’t matter who goes on the left or right because each term is both sufficient and necessary. Whenever you have a double arrow, you can switch who’s on the left and right at will. This is why you don’t have to flip the conditional when you negate it in the contrapositive.

IF AND ONLY IF FAMILY

if but only if, all and only, but not otherwise, when and only when
